verses.sanskrit: अथ प्रथमोऽध्यायः॥ ॐ अथातो ब्रह्मजिज्ञासा ॐ
verses.transliteration: atha prathamo.adhyAyaH|| OM athAto brahmajij~nAsA OM
verses.translation: Now, therefore, the inquiry into Brahman.
verses.hindi: अब, इसलिए, ब्रह्म की जिज्ञासा (अन्वेषण) करें।
verses.wordMeaning: Four words that open the entire Vedanta tradition. "Atha" (now) — this inquiry cannot be postponed. "Ataḥ" (therefore) — because human life is finite and the highest question demands attention. "Brahma" — the ultimate reality, consciousness, the ground of all existence. "Jijñāsā" — not doctrine or belief but living inquiry, open investigation.

verses.translation: That from which the origin, sustenance, and dissolution of this (universe) proceed — that is Brahman.
verses.hindi: जिससे इस जगत की उत्पत्ति, स्थिति और प्रलय होती है — वह ब्रह्म है।
verses.wordMeaning: The Brahma Sutra's definition of Brahman is functional, not theological: Brahman is identified by what it does — creates, sustains, and dissolves all existence. This is not a claim about a deity; it is a philosophical pointer to the ground of existence itself. Whatever underlies and enables the entire process of the universe — that is what Vyasa means by Brahman.

verses.translation: Because the scriptures are the source (of valid knowledge of Brahman).
verses.hindi: क्योंकि शास्त्र (वेद-उपनिषद) ब्रह्मज्ञान का स्रोत हैं।
verses.wordMeaning: Brahman cannot be known through ordinary perception or logical inference alone — the testimony of those who have directly realised it (the Upanishadic seers) is a necessary means of knowledge. This is not blind faith — it is epistemological precision. Just as you need specialised instruments to measure gamma rays, you need the "instrument" of authoritative testimony for knowledge that lies beyond ordinary cognitive reach.

verses.translation: But that (Brahman) — through harmonisation (of all scriptural teachings).
verses.hindi: परंतु वह (ब्रह्म) — समन्वय (समन्वित अनुशीलन) से जाना जाता है।
verses.commentary: One of the Brahma Sutra's most important methodological sutras: the path to Brahman is through the harmonious synthesis of all scriptural teachings — not selective quotation, not sectarian emphasis. 'Samanvaya' means 'bringing together into harmony.' The truth is found not in any one teaching but in the pattern that all authentic teachings share when viewed together.

verses.translation: On account of seeing (consciousness), primordial matter is not the first cause (as it has no self-awareness).
verses.hindi: देखने (दर्शन/ईक्षण) के कारण, प्रधान (जड़ प्रकृति) प्रथम कारण नहीं हो सकती।
verses.commentary: Vyasa's refutation of Samkhya philosophy's claim that inert Prakriti (primordial matter) is the first cause of the universe. The Brahma Sutra argues: the Upanishads say the first cause 'saw' (ikshata) before creating. Inert matter cannot see — only consciousness can. Therefore, consciousness, not matter, is the first cause. This is the foundational argument of idealist Vedanta.

verses.translation: If "seeing" is said to be used in a figurative sense — no, because of the word "Self" (used of the cause).
Because liberation is taught for one who is devoted to that (Being).
And because it is not stated that it (the Being) is to be rejected.
Because of the merging into its own Self (of the individual, in deep sleep).
Because of the uniformity of the scriptural statements (about the cause of the world).
And because (its being a conscious cause) is stated in scripture.
The inner Self is bliss (anandamaya) — on account of repetition (in the Upanishads).
verses.hindi: आनन्दमय (आत्मा ही आनन्दमय है) — क्योंकि उपनिषदों में इसकी बार-बार पुष्टि है।
verses.commentary: The Brahma Sutra establishes, through the repetition method (abhyasa), that the innermost Self (Anandamaya) is not merely a sheath of bliss but is identical with Brahman itself. The deepest layer of the person is not suffering, not limitation, not a separate ego — it is pure ananda (bliss). This is a constitutional claim about the nature of consciousness: its ground state is bliss, not pain.

verses.translation: If it be said that the Blissful is not the Supreme because the word denotes a modification (-maya) — no, because the suffix denotes abundance.
And because it is declared to be the cause of that (bliss).
And that same (Brahman) is sung of in the mantra portion of the Veda.
Not the other (the individual soul), because that is not possible.
And because of the declaration of difference (between the two).
And because of (the mention of) desire, there is no need to look for an inferred (Pradhana as cause).

verses.sanskrit: ॐ अस्मिन्नस्य च तद्योगं शास्ति ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM asminnasya cha tadyogaM shAsti OM
verses.translation: And scripture teaches the union of this (individual soul) with that (Blissful One) in it.
The one within (the sun and the eye) is the Lord, because of the teaching of his attributes.
And he is another than the individual soul, because of the declaration of difference.
Space (akasha) is Brahman, because of its characteristic marks.
For that very reason, prana (the vital principle in the text) is also Brahman.
The light (in the text) is Brahman, because of the mention of "feet" in the context.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ छन्दोऽभिधानान्नेतिचेन्न तथाचेतोऽर्पणनिगदात्तथा हि दर्शनम् ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM Chando.abhidhAnAnnetichenna tathAcheto.arpaNanigadAttathA hi darshanam OM
verses.translation: If it be said that it is not Brahman because a metre (Gayatri) is mentioned — no, since the directing of the mind on Brahman through the metre is thus taught; and so it is seen elsewhere.
And thus the statement of the (four) feet as beings and so on is also justified.
If it be said that it is not so because of a difference in the teaching — no, because in both statements there is no contradiction.
Prana is Brahman, because of the connection (of the context) thus.
If it be said that it is not Brahman because the speaker (Indra) teaches about himself — (we reply) no, for there is abundant reference to the Self in this chapter.
The teaching (by Indra) is given through insight from scripture, as in the case of Vamadeva.

If it be said that it is not Brahman because of marks of the individual soul and the chief breath — no, because of the threefold nature of the meditation (on the soul, on the breath, on Brahman), and because those marks are here taken up on that basis.

verses.sanskrit: इति श्रीमत्कृष्णद्वैपायनकृतब्रह्मसूत्रेषु प्रथमाध्यायस्य प्रथमः पादः समाप्तः ॐ सर्वत्र प्रसिद्धोपदेशात् ॐ
verses.transliteration: iti shrImatkR^iShNadvaipAyanakR^itabrahmasUtreShu prathamAdhyAyasya prathamaH pAdaH samAptaH OM sarvatra prasiddhopadeshAt OM
verses.translation: (The one made of mind is Brahman,) because of the teaching of what is well known everywhere (in the Upanishads as the object of meditation).
And because the qualities intended to be taught are appropriate (to Brahman).
But not the embodied soul, because those qualities are not possible for it.
And because of the declaration of object and agent (the one to be attained and the attainer).
Because of the difference of case-endings (in the text).
And because of the Smriti.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ अर्भकौकस्त्वात् तद्व्यपदेशाच्च नेति चेन्न निचाय्यत्वादेवं व्योमवच्च ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM arbhakaukastvAt tadvyapadeshAchcha neti chenna nichAyyatvAdevaM vyomavachcha OM
verses.translation: If it be said that it is not Brahman because of the smallness of its abode and because it is so declared — no, because (it is so) for the sake of meditation, and (it is great) like space.
If it be said that (Brahman) would then have experience of enjoyment — no, because of the difference (between the natures of the two).
The eater is Brahman, because of the mention of the moving and the unmoving (as his food).
And because of the context.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ गुहां प्रविष्टावात्मानौ हि तद्दर्शनात् ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM guhAM praviShTAvAtmAnau hi taddarshanAt OM
verses.translation: The two that have entered the cave are the two selves (the individual and the Supreme), because it is seen thus.
And because of the qualifying terms.
The one within (the eye) is Brahman, because that is appropriate.
And because of the mention of place and the like.
And because of the mention of one characterised by bliss.
And because of the mention of the path of one who has learned the secret teaching.
The other (the reflection, or the soul) is not meant, because of its lack of permanence and the impossibility (of those qualities).
The inner controller in the (texts concerning) the gods and so on is Brahman, because of the declaration of his attributes.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ न च स्मार्तं अतद्धर्माभिपालात् ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM na cha smArtaM ataddharmAbhipAlAt OM
verses.translation: And it is not the (Pradhana) of the Smriti, because attributes not belonging to it are stated.
And the embodied soul is not (the inner controller); for both (recensions) speak of him as different.
The one with the qualities of invisibility and so on is Brahman, because of the statement of his attributes.
The other two (the soul and Pradhana) are not meant, because of the qualifications and the declaration of difference.
And because of the mention of (his) form.
Vaishvanara is Brahman, because of the specific qualifications of the common term.
What is remembered in Smriti would be an indication (of what the Vedic text says).

verses.sanskrit: ॐ शब्दादिभ्योऽन्तः प्रतिष्ठानान्नेति चेन्न तथा दृष्ट्युपदेशादसंभवात्पुरुषविध्मपि चैनमधीयते ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM shabdAdibhyo.antaH pratiShThAnAnneti chenna tathA dR^iShTyupadeshAdasaMbhavAtpuruShavidhmapi chainamadhIyate OM
verses.translation: If it be said that it is not Brahman because of the words (agni and so on) and because it is described as established within — no, because it is taught as an object of meditation, because (otherwise) it would be impossible, and because they also teach him as having the form of a person.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ अत एव न देवता भूतं च ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM ata eva na devatA bhUtaM cha OM
verses.translation: For this very reason Vaishvanara is neither a deity nor an element.
Jaimini says that meditation directly on Brahman as Vaishvanara also involves no contradiction.
Ashmarathya holds that it is because of manifestation (in the worshipper).
Badari holds that it is because of remembrance (in meditation).

verses.sanskrit: ॐ सम्पत्तेरिति जैमिनिः तथा हि दर्शयति ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM sampatteriti jaiminiH tathA hi darshayati OM
verses.translation: Jaimini holds that it is because of (symbolic) identification; for thus (scripture) shows.
And they teach him as (located) in this (body).

verses.sanskrit: इति श्रीमत्कृष्णद्वैपायनकृतब्रह्मसूत्रेषु प्रथमाध्यायस्य द्वितीयः पादः समाप्तः ॐ द्युभ्वाद्यायतनं स्वशब्दात् ॐ
verses.transliteration: iti shrImatkR^iShNadvaipAyanakR^itabrahmasUtreShu prathamAdhyAyasya dvitIyaH pAdaH samAptaH OM dyubhvAdyAyatanaM svashabdAt OM
verses.translation: The abode of heaven, earth and so on is Brahman, because of the word "own" (the Self).
Because it is declared to be the goal to be reached by the liberated.
Not the inferred (Pradhana), because there is no word denoting it.
Nor the individual soul.
Because of the declaration of difference.
Because of the context.
And because of the mention of abiding and eating (one looking on, the other eating).
The Infinite (Bhuma) is Brahman, because of the teaching (of it) beyond the state of deep sleep.
And because its attributes are appropriate (to Brahman).
The Imperishable is Brahman, because it upholds everything up to space.
And that upholding is by (Brahman), because of the ruling (mentioned).
And because it excludes other natures.
He (the Supreme) is the object of seeing, according to the declaration of the text.
The small (space in the heart) is Brahman, because of the subsequent statements.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ गतिशब्दाभ्यां तथा हि दृष्टं लिङ्गं च ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM gatishabdAbhyAM tathA hi dR^iShTaM li~NgaM cha OM
verses.translation: Because of the "going" and the word (Brahman-world); for thus it is seen, and there is also an indication.
And because of the supporting (of the worlds) and because its greatness is perceived in it.
And because of well-known usage.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ इतरपरामर्शात् स इति चेन्नासम्भवात् ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM itaraparAmarshAt sa iti chennAsambhavAt OM
verses.translation: If it be said that it is the individual soul because of the reference to the other, no, because that is impossible.
If it be said that (the individual is meant) because of the later text — (we say) it refers to the soul with its true nature manifested.
And the reference (to the soul) serves another purpose.
If it be said that (it cannot be Brahman) because of the mention of smallness, that has been answered.
(The luminous one) follows (Brahman), and this whole (world) shines by its light.
This too is stated in the Smriti.

verses.sanskrit: पाठभेद अपि च स्मर्यते ॐ शब्दादेव प्रमितः ॐ
verses.transliteration: pAThabheda api cha smaryate OM shabdAdeva pramitaH OM
verses.translation: The one of the measure of a thumb is Brahman, because of the word itself.
It is with reference to the heart, and because human beings alone are eligible (for such knowledge).
Badarayana holds that (beings) above them (the gods) are also eligible, because it is possible.
If it be said that (the bodies of the gods) contradict sacrificial action — no, because of the assuming of many forms, as is seen.
If it be said that (there is a contradiction) with the Vedic word — no, because from it (the world) originates, as shown by direct revelation and Smriti.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ अत एव च नित्यत्वम् ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM ata eva cha nityatvam OM
verses.translation: For this very reason, the eternity (of the Veda) also.
Because of the sameness of names and forms, there is no contradiction even in the recurrence (of creation), as shown by Sruti and Smriti.
Jaimini holds that the gods are not eligible (for Brahma-knowledge), because it is impossible in the case of meditations such as the Madhu-vidya.
And because (the gods) are found in the sphere of light.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ भावं तु बादरायणोऽस्ति हि ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM bhAvaM tu bAdarAyaNo.asti hi OM
verses.translation: But Badarayana holds that (eligibility) exists, for (it is possible).
The word "shuc" (grief) in Janashruti's case is hinted at by his hearing the contemptuous remark and by his running to (Raikva).
And since he is known to be a Kshatriya, from the mention of Chaitraratha later on.
Because of the mention of purificatory rites, and because their absence is stated (in the case of Satyakama).
And because he was taken up (for teaching) upon ascertaining the absence of that (Shudra-hood).
Because hearing, studying and understanding the meaning are forbidden (to Shudras), and because of the Smriti.
(The all-moving life is Brahman,) because of the trembling (of the whole world).
The light (is Brahman), because it is seen (in the text).
Space (in the text) is Brahman, because of the declaration that it is different in nature and so on.
Because of the difference (of the Self from the soul) in deep sleep and in departure.
Because of words such as "lord."

verses.sanskrit: इति श्रीमत्कृष्णद्वैपायनकृतब्रह्मसूत्रेषु प्रथमाध्यायस्य तृतीयः पादः समाप्तः ॐ आनुमानिकमप्येकेषामिति चेन्न शरीररूपकविन्यस्तगृहीतेर्दर्शयति च ॐ
verses.transliteration: iti shrImatkR^iShNadvaipAyanakR^itabrahmasUtreShu prathamAdhyAyasya tR^itIyaH pAdaH samAptaH OM AnumAnikamapyekeShAmiti chenna sharIrarUpakavinyastagR^ihIterdarshayati cha OM
verses.translation: If it be said that even the inferred (Pradhana) is found in some recensions — no, because what is mentioned is the body, imagined as a chariot; and the text shows this.
But the subtle (is the causal body), because it is fit to be so called.
(Its existence is admitted) because it depends on the Lord; it serves a purpose.
And because it is not said to be an object of knowledge.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ वदतीति चेन्न प्राज्ञो हि ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM vadatIti chenna prAj~no hi OM
verses.translation: If it be said that (the text) declares it (as an object of knowledge) — no, for (the text speaks of) the Supreme Self.

verses.sanskrit: पाठभेद 1.4.5 and 6 combined ॐ प्रकरणात् ॐ
verses.transliteration: pAThabheda ## 1.4.5 and 6 combined ## OM prakaraNAt OM
verses.translation: Because of the context (the object of knowledge is the Supreme Self).
Of three things only is there such a statement and question (not of the Pradhana).
And (as in the case of) the "great."
(The "unborn" is not the Sankhya Pradhana,) because there is no specification, as in the case of the (Vedic) cup.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ ज्योतिरुपक्रमा तु तथा ह्यधीयत एके ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM jyotirupakramA tu tathA hyadhIyata eke OM
verses.translation: But (the "unborn") begins with light (Brahman), for so some read.
And because imagining is taught, there is no contradiction, as in the case of the honey (of the sun) and the like.
Nor (does it refer to the Sankhya categories) from the mention of a number, because of the diversity and because of the excess.
Prana and the rest (are Brahman's attributes), because of the remainder of the sentence.
In some recensions, where food is not mentioned, (the five are counted) by means of light.
And Brahman is taught as the cause in the texts about space and the rest, as stated.
Because of the drawing together (of the earlier and later texts).
Because "work" denotes the world.
If it be said that it is not Brahman because of marks of the individual soul and the chief breath, that has been explained.

verses.sanskrit: (जीवमुख्यप्राणलिङ्गादिति) ॐ अन्यार्थं तु जैमिनिः प्रश्नव्याख्यानाभ्यामपि चैवमेके ॐ
verses.transliteration: (jIvamukhyaprANali~NgAditi) OM anyArthaM tu jaiminiH prashnavyAkhyAnAbhyAmapi chaivameke OM
verses.translation: Jaimini holds that the reference (to the soul) is for another purpose, because of the question and the answer; and so some also read.
Because of the connection of the sentences.
Ashmarathya thinks the mention (of the soul) is a mark (of the identity of soul and Brahman), for the proof of the proposition.
Audulomi says it is because of such a state on the soul's departure (from the body).
Kashakritsna says it is because (Brahman) abides (as the soul).
Brahman is also the material cause, because this does not contradict the proposition and the illustration.
And because of the teaching of reflection (in creation).
And because both (origin and dissolution) are directly stated (as from Brahman).
Because it made itself, through transformation.
And because (Brahman) is described as the source (womb).
By this all (other views) are explained; explained.

verses.sanskrit: अथ द्वितीयोऽध्यायः॥ ॐ स्मृत्यनवकाशदोषप्रसङ्ग इति चेन्नान्यस्मृत्यनवकाशदोषप्रसङ्गात् ॐ
verses.transliteration: atha dvitIyo.adhyAyaH|| OM smR^ityanavakAshadoShaprasa~Nga iti chennAnyasmR^ityanavakAshadoShaprasa~NgAt OM
verses.translation: If it be said that (this view) leaves no room for certain Smritis (Kapila's), we reply: no, because (rejecting the other view) would leave no room for other Smritis (Manu's and the like).
And because the other (Sankhya) principles are not found in the Veda.
By this the Yoga system is also refuted.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ न विलक्षणत्वादस्य तथात्वं च शब्दात् ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM na vilakShaNatvAdasya tathAtvaM cha shabdAt OM
verses.translation: (Objection:) Brahman cannot be the cause of this world, because of its being of a different nature; and so the word (of scripture) says.
But (such cases of the unlike arising from the unlike) are seen.
But the mention (of earth, water and so on as speaking) refers to their presiding deities, because of the specific mention and because of (the deities') entering.
And it is seen (that the conscious gives rise to the unconscious, as hair and nails from a man).

verses.sanskrit: पाठभेद दृश्यते तु ॐ असदिति चेन्न प्रतिषेधमात्रत्वात् ॐ
verses.transliteration: pAThabheda dR^ishyate tu OM asaditi chenna pratiShedhamAtratvAt OM
verses.translation: If it be said that (the effect) would then be non-existent (before its origin) — no, because that is merely a denial, with no counter-entity.
At dissolution, (the world would impart its qualities to Brahman,) so (your view) is inconsistent.
But not so, because there are examples (of cause and effect differing in nature without such consequence).
And because the same fault applies to your own view.
Reasoning has no fixed footing; one may infer otherwise — but even then there would be the fault of no release.
By this, the views not accepted by the wise (such as atomism) are also explained (and refuted).
If it be said that (the enjoyer's being merged in the cause) would lead to non-distinction (of enjoyer and enjoyed), we say: it may be so, as in the world (like the sea and its waves).
The non-difference of that (effect) from it (the cause) (is known) from the word "origin" (arambhana) and other texts.
And because (the effect) is perceived when the cause exists.
And because the later (effect) exists (in the cause).

verses.sanskrit: ॐ असद्व्यपदेशान्नेति चेन्न धर्मान्तरेण वाक्यशेषात् ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM asadvyapadeshAnneti chenna dharmAntareNa vAkyasheShAt OM
verses.translation: If it be said that (the effect is) not (in the cause) because of the declaration of non-existence — no, because that is by way of a different attribute, as the rest of the passage shows.
Because of reasoning and because of another text.
And like a piece of cloth.
And like the breath and the other functions.
Because of the declaration of the other (the soul as identical with Brahman), (Brahman would be liable to) faults such as not doing good to himself.
But (Brahman is) something more, because of the statement of difference.
And that (objection) does not stand, as with stones and the like.
If it be said that (Brahman is not the cause) because we see the collection of materials — no, because it is like milk.
As with gods and the like, also in the world.
(If Brahman were transformed,) either the whole would be involved, or the texts declaring it to be without parts would be violated.
But not so, because scripture (says so), and Brahman is known from the word (scripture) alone.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ आत्मनि चैवं विचित्राश्च हि ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM Atmani chaivaM vichitrAshcha hi OM
verses.translation: And in the Self also (such changes are possible), for there are many wonders of this kind.
And because of faults in your own view.
And Brahman is endowed with all powers, because that is seen (in scripture).
If it be said that (Brahman) has no organs, that has been answered.
(Objection:) Brahman is not the creator, because he would then have a purpose.
But (creation is) mere sport, as in the world.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ वैष्यम्यनैर्घृण्ये न सापेक्षत्वात्तथा हि दर्शयति ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM vaiShyamyanairghR^iNye na sApekShatvAttathA hi darshayati OM
verses.translation: Partiality and cruelty do not attach to Brahman, because he acts in regard to (the beings' own karma); so scripture shows.
If it be said that (this is not possible) because of the non-distinction of works (before creation) — no, because (the world) is beginningless.
(The beginninglessness) is reasonable and is also found (in scripture).
And because all attributes are appropriate (to Brahman as cause).

verses.sanskrit: इति श्रीमत्कृष्णद्वैपायनकृतब्रह्मसूत्रेषु द्वितीयाध्यायस्य प्रथमः पादः समाप्तः ॐ रचनानुपपत्तेश्च नानुमानम् ॐ
verses.transliteration: iti shrImatkR^iShNadvaipAyanakR^itabrahmasUtreShu dvitIyAdhyAyasya prathamaH pAdaH samAptaH OM rachanAnupapatteshcha nAnumAnam OM
verses.translation: The inferred (Pradhana) is not the cause, because of the impossibility of the (world's) orderly arrangement.
And because of the (Pradhana's) activity.
If it be said that (it acts) like milk or water, (we reply) even there (a guiding agent is needed).
And because (the Pradhana) has no fixed relation to (the qualities), being independent.
And because (such a process) is not found elsewhere, it is not like grass and the like.
Even if (its activity) is admitted, there would be no purpose.
If it be said (it works) like the lame man and the blind man, or like a magnet — even so (the difficulty remains).
Because a relation of principal and subordinate is not possible (among the qualities).
And even if it is inferred otherwise, the Pradhana lacks the power of intelligence.
And because of contradictions, (the Sankhya doctrine) is inconsistent.
(The Vaisheshika doctrine:) as the great and the long come from the short and the spherical (atoms) — (this too is refuted).
In both ways, the (initial) action of the atoms is not possible; therefore there is no (creation from them).
And because inherence is admitted, and because of similarity, there would be an infinite regress.
And because (the atoms) would then be always active (or always inactive).
And because (the atoms) have colour and so on, the opposite (of their eternity) follows, as is seen.
And because of faults in both cases.
And because (the doctrine) is not accepted (by the wise), it is to be utterly disregarded.
Even if the aggregate is held to have two causes (atoms and their combinations), the aggregate cannot be formed.
If it be said (that the aggregate arises) through the mutual dependence of (ignorance and the rest) — no, because these are only causes of origin.
And because, when the later arises, the former has ceased.
If (the cause) is non-existent (at the time of the effect), the proposition is contradicted; otherwise there would be simultaneity.
Neither conscious nor unconscious destruction is possible, because of the non-interruption (of the series).
And because of faults in both cases.
And in the case of space also (it cannot be called mere non-existence), because of no difference.
And because of memory.
(Existence) does not come from non-existence, because that is not seen.
And thus (origin from non-existence) would hold even for the indifferent (the inactive).
There is no non-existence (of external things), because they are perceived.
And because of the difference in nature, (waking perception is) not like dreams and the like.
(The idealist says) there is no (external) existence, for want of perception — (this is answered).
And because of momentariness (there is no memory and no continuity).
And because (the doctrine) is untenable in every way.
(The Jain view is) not (tenable), because contradictory attributes cannot be in one thing.
And thus the Self would be of imperfect nature (not whole).

verses.sanskrit: ॐ न च पर्यायादप्यविरोधः विकारादिभ्यः ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM na cha paryAyAdapyavirodhaH vikArAdibhyaH OM
verses.translation: Nor is there non-contradiction by turns, because of change and so on.
And because the final size of the soul is permanent, and both (the initial and final) are permanent, there is no distinction.
(The Pashupata view of God as the instrumental cause only is untenable,) because of inconsistency in the Lord.
And because of the impossibility of a relation.
And because of the impossibility of guiding (the world).
If it be said (he directs) like an instrument — no, because (he would then experience) enjoyment and the like.
(He would then be) finite, or not omniscient.
Because of the impossibility of origin (of the soul from Sankarshana).

verses.sanskrit: ॐ न च कर्तुः करणम् ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM na cha kartuH karaNam OM
verses.translation: And the instrument does not originate from the agent.
Or if (the four forms) are endowed with knowledge and the like, the objection is not removed.
And because of contradictions.

verses.sanskrit: इति श्रीमत्कृष्णद्वैपायनकृतब्रह्मसूत्रेषु द्वितीयाध्यायस्य द्वितीयः पादः समाप्तः ॐ न वियदश्रुतेः ॐ
verses.transliteration: iti shrImatkR^iShNadvaipAyanakR^itabrahmasUtreShu dvitIyAdhyAyasya dvitIyaH pAdaH samAptaH OM na viyadashruteH OM
verses.translation: Space is not produced, because there is no scriptural statement of it.
But there is (such a statement).
(The statement about space's origin) cannot be figurative, because that is impossible.
And because of the text.
And the (word "born") may apply to one thing in two senses, as with the word "Brahman."
(Otherwise) the proposition (that by knowing one all is known) would fail; the texts show the non-difference (of effects from Brahman).

verses.sanskrit: ॐ यावद्विकारं तु विभागो लोकवत् ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM yAvadvikAraM tu vibhAgo lokavat OM
verses.translation: But the division (of things) extends as far as modifications, as in the world.
By this, air (Matarishvan) is explained.
But the origin of the Existent (Brahman) is impossible, because it is unreasonable.
Fire (arises) from that (air), for so the text says.
Water (arises from fire).
Earth (arises from water), because of the context, the colour (mentioned) and other texts.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ तदभिध्यानादेव तु तल्लिङ्गात् सः ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM tadabhidhyAnAdeva tu talli~NgAt saH OM
verses.translation: (The creation proceeds) from that (Brahman) alone, by his reflection, because of the indication.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ विपर्ययेण तु क्रमोऽत उपपद्यते च ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM viparyayeNa tu kramo.ata upapadyate cha OM
verses.translation: The order of dissolution is the reverse of that of creation; this is also reasonable.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ अन्तरा विज्ञानमनसी क्रमेण तल्लिङ्गादिति चेन्नाविशेषात् ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM antarA vij~nAnamanasI krameNa talli~NgAditi chennAvisheShAt OM
verses.translation: If it be said that intellect and mind come in between (the elements) in order, because of the indication — no, because of no specification.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ चराचरव्यपाश्रयस्तु स्यात् तद्व्यपदेशो भाक्तः तद्भावभावित्वात् ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM charAcharavyapAshrayastu syAt tadvyapadesho bhAktaH tadbhAvabhAvitvAt OM
verses.translation: The expressions of birth and death (concerning the soul) refer to bodies, moving and unmoving; they are figurative, because they hold only while the body exists.
The soul is not produced, because there is no such statement, and because the texts declare its eternity.
For this very reason the soul is a knower.
And because of reasoning.
(The soul is atomic, says the objector,) because of its departure, going and coming.
And the latter two (going and coming) are by its own self.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ नाणुरतत् श्रुतेरिति चेन्न इतराधिकारात् ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM nANuratat shruteriti chenna itarAdhikArAt OM
verses.translation: If it be said that it is not atomic because of texts to the contrary — no, because those refer to the other (the Supreme Self).
And by direct statement and by measurement.
There is no contradiction, as with sandal paste.
If it be said that (the soul pervades the body) because of its being found in a particular place — no, because of the admitted (location) in the heart.
Or (it pervades) by its quality (consciousness), like light.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ व्यतिरेको गन्धवत् तथा च दर्शयति ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM vyatireko gandhavat tathA cha darshayati OM
verses.translation: The quality extends beyond (its substance), like fragrance; and so scripture shows.
Because of the separate mention (of the knower and the knowledge).
But it is called atomic because the qualities of the intellect predominate in it, like the Supreme (in the "Prajna" text).
And there is no fault, since the connection (with the intellect) lasts as long as the soul (is in worldly existence), as scripture shows.
It is like maleness and the like: existing (as latent), it becomes manifest at the proper time.
Otherwise there would be either constant perception or constant non-perception, or a restriction to one of the two.
The soul is an agent, because scripture has meaning (its injunctions are addressed to an agent).
Because of the teaching of its roaming.
Because of its taking up (the organs).

verses.sanskrit: ॐ व्यपदेशाच्च क्रियायां न चेन्निर्देशविपर्ययः ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM vyapadeshAchcha kriyAyAM na chennirdeshaviparyayaH OM
verses.translation: And because of the declaration about action; otherwise the statement would be reversed.
As in the case of perception, there is no fixed rule (of agency).
Because of the reversal of powers (if the intellect were the agent).
And because of the impossibility of absorption (samadhi).
And as the carpenter (is agent) in both ways (working with tools and resting).
But (the soul's agency is) from the Supreme, because the text says so.
But (the Lord acts) with regard to the effort made by the soul, so that injunctions and prohibitions are not meaningless.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ अंशो नानाव्यपदेशादन्यथा चापि दाशकितवादित्वमधीयत एके ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM aMsho nAnAvyapadeshAdanyathA chApi dAshakitavAditvamadhIyata eke OM
verses.translation: The soul is a part of the Lord, because of the various declarations (of difference and non-difference); and because some read (Brahman) as "slaves, rogues" and so on.
Because of the mantra.
It is also stated in the Smriti.

verses.sanskrit: पाठभेद अपि च स्मर्यते ॐ प्रकाशादिवन्नैवं परः ॐ
verses.transliteration: pAThabheda api cha smaryate OM prakAshAdivannaivaM paraH OM
verses.translation: The Supreme is not affected thus (by the soul's sorrow), like light and the like.
And the Smriti says so.
Injunction and prohibition apply because of the connection with a body, as in the case of fire and the like.
And because (the soul) is not all-pervading, there is no confusion (of the results of actions).
(The individual soul is) only a reflection (of the Supreme).
Because of the non-regulation of unseen merit (on the other view).
And so also with intention and the like.
If it be said that (the regulation is) by place — no, because (all souls) are included (in each).

verses.sanskrit: इति श्रीमत्कृष्णद्वैपायनकृतब्रह्मसूत्रेषु द्वितीयाध्यायस्य तृतीयः पादः समाप्तः ॐ तथा प्राणाः ॐ
verses.transliteration: iti shrImatkR^iShNadvaipAyanakR^itabrahmasUtreShu dvitIyAdhyAyasya tR^itIyaH pAdaH samAptaH OM tathA prANAH OM
verses.translation: Likewise, the vital breaths (organs) are produced.
(Their origin) cannot be figurative, because that is impossible.
And because the proposition is not contradicted.

verses.sanskrit: पाठभेद sUtra absent ॐ तत्प्राक्श्रुतेश्च ॐ
verses.translation: And because scripture speaks (of the organs) before that (their origin is mentioned).
Because speech (as an organ) is preceded by (depends on) that.
The organs are seven, because of their going (with the soul) and because of specification.
But hands and the like are (additional), since they exist; so it is not thus (only seven).
And they are minute.
And the chief (breath) too.
It is neither air nor a function of it, because of the separate mention.
But it is like the eye and the like (subordinate to the soul), because of being taught along with them and so on.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ अकरणत्वाच्च न दोषस्तथा हि दर्शयति ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM akaraNatvAchcha na doShastathA hi darshayati OM
verses.translation: And since it is not an instrument (of knowledge), there is no fault; so scripture shows.
It is described as having five functions, like the mind.
And it is minute.
But (the organs are) governed by fire and other deities, because scripture teaches it.
(They are connected) with the one who has life (the soul), because of the text.
And because of the permanence of that (connection).

verses.sanskrit: ॐ त इन्द्रियाणि तद्व्यपदेशादन्यत्र श्रेष्ठात् ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM ta indriyANi tadvyapadeshAdanyatra shreShThAt OM
verses.translation: These are the senses, so called except the chief (breath), because of the designation.
Because scripture speaks of the difference.
And because of the difference in nature.
But the making of names and forms is by him who makes (the elements) threefold, because of the teaching.
Flesh and the like come from earth, according to the text; and (so for the other two elements) also.
But because of the preponderance (of a particular element), the special designation of each; the designation.

verses.sanskrit: अथ तृतीयोऽध्यायः॥ ॐ तदन्तरप्रतिपत्तौ रंहति सम्परिष्वक्तः प्रश्ननिरूपणाभ्याम् ॐ
verses.transliteration: atha tR^itIyo.adhyAyaH|| OM tadantarapratipattau raMhati sampariShvaktaH prashnanirUpaNAbhyAm OM
verses.translation: In passing to another body, the soul goes enveloped by (subtle elements), as is clear from the question and the answer.
(Water is named in the question) because the (body-forming) elements are threefold in nature, but water preponderates.
And because of the going of the vital breath (with the soul).
If it be said that the going of speech and the rest to fire and so on is stated (so that the soul does not carry the elements) — no, because that is figurative.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ प्रथमेऽश्रवणादिति चेन्न ता एव ह्युपपत्तेः ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM prathame.ashravaNAditi chenna tA eva hyupapatteH OM
verses.translation: If it be said that water is not mentioned in the first oblation — no, because "water" there is faith, which is appropriate.
If it be said that (the soul's going with water) is not stated — no, because it is understood of those who perform sacrifices and the like.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ भाक्तं वाऽनात्मवित्त्वात् तथा हि दर्शयति ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM bhAktaM vA.anAtmavittvAt tathA hi darshayati OM
verses.translation: Or (the statement that they are food for the gods) is figurative, because they do not know the Self; so scripture shows.
When their works are exhausted, souls return with a remainder of karma, as Sruti and Smriti show.

verses.sanskrit: पाठभेद 3.1.8 and 9 combined ॐ यथेतमनेवं च ॐ
verses.transliteration: pAThabheda ## 3.1.8 and 9 combined## OM yathetamanevaM cha OM
verses.translation: (They return) by the path by which they went, and also otherwise.
If it be said that (birth is) by conduct — no; conduct is only indicative, says Karshnajini.
If it be said that (works) would then be useless — no, because conduct depends on them.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ सुकृतदुष्कृते एवेति तु बादरिः ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM sukR^itaduShkR^ite eveti tu bAdariH OM
verses.translation: Badari holds that (the remainder) is only good and evil works.
And it is also stated (that) those who do evil and the like (go to the moon).
But the others, having experienced (suffering) in the realm of Yama, ascend and descend, since their going is so described.
And the Smriti says so.
There are also seven (hells).
Even there, there is no contradiction, since (Yama's servants) preside there.
But (the two paths) are for those of knowledge and works, because they are the subject.
Not so with the third place, for it is described thus.
It is also stated in the Smriti, in the world.
And because of what is seen.
The third (place) is included in the word (for creatures born of sweat and the like).
And because of the Smriti.
(The soul attains) likeness in nature to (space, wind and so on), because that is appropriate.
Not after a very long time (does it descend), because of the specification.
(It enters) plants presided over by other souls, as in the earlier stages, because of the statement.
If it be said that (the sacrifice) is impure (because it involves killing) — no, because of the scriptural word.
Then (comes) union with the one who sheds semen.
From the womb, a body.

verses.sanskrit: इति श्रीमत्कृष्णद्वैपायनकृतब्रह्मसूत्रेषु तृतीयाध्यायस्य प्रथमः पादः समाप्तः ॐ सन्ध्ये सृष्टिराह हि ॐ
verses.transliteration: iti shrImatkR^iShNadvaipAyanakR^itabrahmasUtreShu tR^itIyAdhyAyasya prathamaH pAdaH samAptaH OM sandhye sR^iShTirAha hi OM
verses.translation: In the dream state there is creation, for scripture says so.
Some recensions speak of the Self as the creator of sons and other desired objects.
But it is mere illusion, because its nature is not fully manifest (as in waking).

verses.sanskrit: ॐ सूचकश्च हि श्रुतेः आचक्षते च तद्विदः ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM sUchakashcha hi shruteH AchakShate cha tadvidaH OM
verses.translation: And it is an indicator (of future events), according to scripture; and those who know dream-lore say so.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ पराभिध्यानात्तु तिरोहितं ततो ह्यस्य बन्धविपर्ययौ ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM parAbhidhyAnAttu tirohitaM tato hyasya bandhaviparyayau OM
verses.translation: But that (the soul's lordship) is hidden by the will of the Supreme; hence its bondage and the reverse.
(The concealment is) also owing to the connection with the body.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ तदभावो नाडीषु तच्छ्रुतेः आत्मनि च ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM tadabhAvo nADIShu tachChruteH Atmani cha OM
verses.translation: The absence of dreams (in deep sleep) is in the channels and in the Self, according to scripture.
Hence the awakening is from that (Self).

verses.sanskrit: ॐ स एव तु कर्मानुस्मृतिशब्दविधिभ्यः ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM sa eva tu karmAnusmR^itishabdavidhibhyaH OM
verses.translation: The same (soul awakens), because of the memory of deeds, the text and the injunction.
In the swoon there is half-attainment (of deep sleep), by elimination.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ न स्थानतोऽपि परस्योभयलिङ्गं सर्वत्र हि ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM na sthAnato.api parasyobhayali~NgaM sarvatra hi OM
verses.translation: Not even by reason of place can the Supreme have twofold characteristics, for everywhere (scripture describes him as without qualities).

verses.sanskrit: ॐ न भेदादिति चेन्न प्रत्येकमतद्वचनात् ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM na bhedAditi chenna pratyekamatadvachanAt OM
verses.translation: If it be said (that he has them) because of differences (in the limiting adjuncts) — no, because each text denies this.
And so some recensions also teach.
For (Brahman) is formless alone, as it is the principal purport of the texts.
And, like light, (it takes forms), so that the texts about forms are not futile.
And scripture says that it is only that (pure consciousness).
And scripture shows this, and it is also stated in the Smriti.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ अत एव चोपमा सूर्यकादिवत् ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM ata eva chopamA sUryakAdivat OM
verses.translation: For this very reason the comparisons (of the Self) with reflections of the sun and the like.
But the comparison is not exact, since (Brahman) is not grasped (as located) like water.
(The comparison holds with respect to) sharing the increase and decrease, because (Brahman) is inside; thus both statements are consistent.
And because scripture shows this.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ प्रकृतैतावत्त्वं हि प्रतिषेधति ततो ब्रवीति च भूयः ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM prakR^itaitAvattvaM hi pratiShedhati tato bravIti cha bhUyaH OM
verses.translation: For (the text) denies the limited extent of what was described, and then says more.
That (Brahman) is unmanifest, for scripture says so.
And (it is perceived) in perfect meditation, as Sruti and Smriti show.
And, like light, there is no difference (between soul and Brahman in their nature).

verses.sanskrit: पाठभेद 3.2.25 and 26 combined ॐ प्रकाशश्च कर्मण्यभ्यासात् ॐ
verses.transliteration: pAThabheda ## 3.2.25 and 26 combined ## OM prakAshashcha karmaNyabhyAsAt OM
verses.translation: And the (soul's) light is shown in action, because of repetition.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ अतोऽनन्तेन तथा हि लिङ्गम् ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM ato.anantena tathA hi li~Ngam OM
verses.translation: Therefore (the soul is united) with the Infinite; for there is an indication of this.
But because of both statements (of difference and of non-difference), it is like a snake and its coils.
Or like light and its substratum, because both are luminous.
Or as in the earlier case.
And because of the denial (of anything else).
(There is something) higher than this (Brahman), (says the objector,) because of the terms "bridge," "measure," "connection" and "difference."
But (they are used) because of similarity.
(The measure) is for the sake of understanding, like the "feet" of Brahman.
(The reference to "connection") is because of particular locations, like light and the like.
And because it is reasonable.
And so, because of the denial of anything else.
By this the all-pervadingness (of Brahman) is established, from words like "extent."
The fruit (of action) comes from him (the Lord), because that is reasonable.
And because scripture says so.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ धर्मं जैमिनिः अत एव ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM dharmaM jaiminiH ata eva OM
verses.translation: Jaimini holds it to be dharma (the work itself), for that very reason.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ पूर्वं तु बादरायणो हेतुव्यपदेशात् ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM pUrvaM tu bAdarAyaNo hetuvyapadeshAt OM
verses.translation: But Badarayana holds the former (the Lord), because he is declared to be the cause.

verses.sanskrit: इति श्रीमत्कृष्णद्वैपायनकृतब्रह्मसूत्रेषु तृतीयाध्यायस्य द्वितीयः पादः समाप्तः ॐ सर्ववेदान्तप्रत्ययं चोदनाद्यविशेषात् ॐ
verses.transliteration: iti shrImatkR^iShNadvaipAyanakR^itabrahmasUtreShu tR^itIyAdhyAyasya dvitIyaH pAdaH samAptaH OM sarvavedAntapratyayaM chodanAdyavisheShAt OM
verses.translation: The meditations mentioned in all the Vedanta texts are the same, because injunctions and the like are not different.
If it be said no, because of differences (in details) — no; even within one (meditation) such differences may occur.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ स्वाध्यायस्य तथात्वेन हि समाचारेऽधिकाराच्च ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM svAdhyAyasya tathAtvena hi samAchAre.adhikArAchcha OM
verses.translation: Because the study (of the Veda) is a duty in that way, and because of the eligibility in the usage (of the followers of the Atharva Veda).

verses.sanskrit: पाठभेद + समाचारेऽधिकाराच्च सववच्च तन्नियमः ॐ सलिलवच्च तन्नियमः ॐ
verses.transliteration: pAThabheda ##+## samAchAre.adhikArAchcha savavachcha tanniyamaH OM salilavachcha tanniyamaH OM
verses.translation: And that rule is like the rule about the water (of the sacrificial cup).
And scripture shows this.
The details are to be combined (in all), because the purport is the same, as with the subordinate parts of an injunction, and in the same (meditation).

verses.sanskrit: ॐ अन्यथात्वं च शब्दादिति चेन्नाविशेषात् ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM anyathAtvaM cha shabdAditi chennAvisheShAt OM
verses.translation: If it be said that it is different because of the text — no, because there is no specific difference.
Or not (the same), because of the difference of context, as with the meditations on the "higher than the highest" and the like.
If it be said that the name shows the identity, that has been answered; and moreover there is (sameness even so).
And because of the pervasiveness (of the Self), it is consistent.
Because of the identity of all (such texts), these (qualities) are to be combined elsewhere.
Bliss and the like belong to the principal (Brahman).
Having a head called "joy" and the like are not to be transferred, because increase and decrease belong to what has difference.
But the others (reality, knowledge, infinity) are to be combined, because of the sameness of meaning.
(The others are) for meditation, because there is no other purpose.
And because of the word "Self."
The Self (the Supreme) is meant, as in other texts, because of the later text.
If it be said (that the Self is the individual) because of the connection — it is (the Supreme), by reason of the definite assertion.
Because (sipping water) is stated as an act, it is something new (an unprecedented rite).
(The meditation) is the same (in all), because of non-difference.
Similarly elsewhere too, because of the connection.
Or not (the same), because of the difference.
And scripture shows this.
The "gathering" and the "pervading of heaven" (qualities) also (belong to Brahman); hence (they are to be combined).
As in the Purusha meditation, so in the others there is no such mention (so they are not to be combined).
Because the mantras of piercing and the like have different purposes.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ हानौ तूपायनशब्दशेषात् कुशाच्छन्दस्स्तुत्युपगानवत् तदुक्तम् ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM hAnau tUpAyanashabdasheShAt kushAchChandasstutyupagAnavat.h taduktam OM
verses.translation: When (good and evil) are shaken off, the "taking up" (is stated) from the remainder of the text — like Kusha grass, metres, praise and singing; this has been explained.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ साम्पराये तर्तव्याभावात् तथा ह्यन्ये ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM sAmparAye tartavyAbhAvAt tathA hyanye OM
verses.translation: At death (good and evil are shed), because there is nothing more to cross; so others also read.
(The going is) at his own will, since there is no contradiction between the two statements.
The soul's going has a purpose in both ways (for the knower of the qualified Brahman); otherwise there is a contradiction.
It is reasonable, since the purpose of the characteristics is found, as in the world.
There is no fixed rule for all knowers; there is no contradiction, as Sruti and Smriti show.
The stay of those charged with offices lasts as long as their office.
But the meditations on the Imperishable are to be combined, because of generality and their being that (Brahman), as in the Upasad — this has been said.
Because so much only is taught (in the text).

verses.sanskrit: ॐ अन्तरा भूतग्रामवदिति चेत् तदुक्तम् ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM antarA bhUtagrAmavaditi chet taduktam OM
verses.translation: (The inner Self is the same) as in the case of the Self within the elements.
If it be said that otherwise the difference would be inexplicable — no, it is like a difference of teaching.
Interchange (of "I" and "thou") is meant, for they specify it as in other cases.
Truth and the like are the same (in the two texts).

verses.sanskrit: ॐ कामादितरत्र तत्र च आयतनादिभ्यः ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM kAmAditaratra tatra cha AyatanAdibhyaH OM
verses.translation: Desires and the like are to be combined in the other place, and there too, because of the abode and so on.
There is no omission (of the rite), because of the respect shown.
(The fulfilment) presents itself, because of the text.
There is no fixed rule as to ascertaining it, because it is seen (in the texts); the fruit is separately unobstructed.
As with a gift, this has been stated.
Because of the greater number of indications, that is stronger; even that (holds).
The former (the mental cups) are alternatives (to the physical rite) because of the context, like the mental rite.
And because of extension (of rules).
But (the fires) are (parts of) knowledge alone, because of the determination.
And because of what is seen (in scripture).
And because of the greater force of direct statement and the like, there is no sublation.
Because of connection and the like.
And the vision (of the fires) is distinct, like the separateness of other kinds of knowledge; this has been said.
Not (identity) even from generality, as it is seen; like death (not being the sun), there is no attainment of the world (by mere similarity).

verses.sanskrit: ॐ परेण च शब्दस्य ताद्विध्यं भूयस्त्वात्त्वनुबन्धः ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM pareNa cha shabdasya tAdvidhyaM bhUyastvAttvanubandhaH OM
verses.translation: And (this holds) for later texts of such kind; the connection is due to the greater number.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ एक आत्मनः शरीरे भावात् ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM eka AtmanaH sharIre bhAvAt OM
verses.translation: Some (deny) the Self's existence apart from the body, because (the self) is found in the body.
(The Self) is distinct (from the body), because (the body's qualities) do not exist in the same way; it is not like perception (which arises with the body).

verses.sanskrit: ॐ अङ्गावबद्धास्तु न शाखासु हि प्रतिवेदम् ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM a~NgAvabaddhAstu na shAkhAsu hi prativedam OM
verses.translation: But the meditations connected with parts (of a rite) are not restricted to particular branches of the Veda, but hold in each Veda.
Or, as with mantras and the like, there is no contradiction.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ भूम्नः क्रतुवज्ज्यायस्त्वं तथा च दर्शयति ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM bhUmnaH kratuvajjyAyastvaM tathA cha darshayati OM
verses.translation: The greater (meditation) is superior, like a sacrifice; and so scripture shows.
(The meditations are) different, because of the difference of words and so on.
(They are) alternatives, because they have the same special result.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ काम्यास्तु यथाकामं समुच्चीयेरन्न वा पूर्वहेत्वभावात् ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM kAmyAstu yathAkAmaM samuchchIyeranna vA pUrvahetvabhAvAt OM
verses.translation: But those (meditations) for desired ends may be combined as one wishes, or not, since the former reason is absent.
In the subordinate parts (of a rite), (the meditations) follow their substrates.
And because of the injunction.
Because of the combining (of the parts).
And because of the statement that the quality is common.
Or not (so), because of the statement of their being together.
And because of what is seen.

verses.sanskrit: इति श्रीमत्कृष्णद्वैपायनकृतब्रह्मसूत्रेषु तृतीयाध्यायस्य तृतीयः पादः समाप्तः ॐ पुरुषार्थोऽतः शब्दादिति बादरायणः ॐ
verses.transliteration: iti shrImatkR^iShNadvaipAyanakR^itabrahmasUtreShu tR^itIyAdhyAyasya tR^itIyaH pAdaH samAptaH OM puruShArtho.ataH shabdAditi bAdarAyaNaH OM
verses.translation: The purpose of man is accomplished by this (knowledge), so Badarayana says, because of the scriptural word.
Jaimini says the statements about human purpose are only praise, since (knowledge) is subordinate (to rites), as in other cases.
Because of the conduct (of knowers) seen in scripture.
Because scripture says so.
Because (knowledge) accompanies (the rite).
Because (rites) are enjoined on one who has that (knowledge).
And because of the rule.
But Badarayana's view is right, because the teaching is of something beyond (rites), as scripture shows.
But the seeing (in the same scripture) is equal on both sides.
It is not universal (that knowledge is subordinate to rites).
There is a division (of the two), like a hundred (divided).
(Rites are enjoined) on one who has merely learnt the text.
Not so, because there is no distinction (in the text).
Or (the mention of works) is a permission, for praise.
And some (are said to act) by choice.
And (scripture speaks of) the destruction (of works).

verses.sanskrit: ॐ ऊर्ध्वरेतस्सु च शब्दे हि ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM Urdhvaretassu cha shabde hi OM
verses.translation: And (this knowledge exists) among those of continent life, for the scripture says so.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ परामर्शं जैमिनिरचोदना चापवदिति हि ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM parAmarshaM jaiminirachodanA chApavaditi hi OM
verses.translation: Jaimini holds (the text) is merely a reference, for it is not an injunction, and scripture decries (it).
Badarayana holds that (the life-stages) are to be practised, because of the equal statement of all.
Or it is an injunction, like the holding (of a fuel-stick).
If it be said that it is merely praise, because of the mention — no, because it is something new.
And because of the word denoting an act to be done.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ पारिप्लवार्था इति चेन्न विशेषितत्वात् ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM pAriplavArthA iti chenna visheShitatvAt OM
verses.translation: If it be said that (the stories) are for the Pariplava recitation — no, because they are specified.
And thus because of their connection in one sentence (with the meditation).
For this very reason there is no need of the fires, fuel and the like.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ सर्वापेक्षा च यज्ञादिश्रुतेः अश्ववत् ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM sarvApekShA cha yaj~nAdishruteH ashvavat OM
verses.translation: But there is need of all (works), because of the texts on sacrifice and the like, as with a horse.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ शमदमाद्युपेतः स्यात्तथाऽपि तु तद्विधेस्तदङ्गतया तेषामवश्यानुष्ठेयत्वात् ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM shamadamAdyupetaH syAttathA.api tu tadvidhestada~NgatayA teShAmavashyAnuShTheyatvAt OM
verses.translation: Yet one should be endowed with calmness, self-control and the like, because these are enjoined as its aids and must be practised.
And permission to eat all kinds of food (holds) only when life is in danger, as is seen (in the story).
And because (this) is not opposed (to the rule).
And it is also stated in the Smriti.
And the scriptural word (forbids) acting by whim.
And the duties of the stages of life are also enjoined.
And (they are) helpful (to knowledge).

verses.sanskrit: ॐ सर्वथापि तु त एवोभयलिङ्गात् ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM sarvathApi tu ta evobhayali~NgAt OM
verses.translation: In any case the same (works) are meant, because of the indication of both Sruti and Smriti.
And (scripture) shows that (the knower) is not overcome.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ अन्तरा चापि तु तद्दृष्टेः ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM antarA chApi tu taddR^iShTeH OM
verses.translation: And (persons standing) between (the stages) are also eligible, as is seen.
And it is stated in the Smriti.
And there is special favour (by the works of the stages).
But the other (the life of the stages) is better, because of the indication.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ तद्भूतस्य तु तद्भावो जैमिनेरपि नियमातद्रूपाऽभावेभ्यः ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM tadbhUtasya tu tadbhAvo jaiminerapi niyamAtadrUpA.abhAvebhyaH OM
verses.translation: But one who has become that (an ascetic) cannot revert, even according to Jaimini, because of the rule and because of the absence of any such permission.
Nor does (the rule of atonement) for one in office (apply), because a fall is inferred and it is unsuitable.
Some regard (this) as a minor sin, like eating (forbidden food); this has been said.
But in both cases (they are) excluded (from society), because of Smriti and usage.
Atreya holds that (the fruit of meditation in a rite) belongs to the master (the sacrificer), because of the statement of fruit.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ आर्त्विज्यमित्यौडुलोमिः तस्मै हि परिक्रियते ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM ArtvijyamityauDulomiH tasmai hi parikriyate OM
verses.translation: Audulomi says it belongs to the priest, because he is paid for it.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ सहकार्यन्तरविधिः पक्षेण तृतीयं तद्वतो विद्यादिवत् ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM sahakAryantaravidhiH pakSheNa tR^itIyaM tadvato vidyAdivat OM
verses.translation: There is an injunction of a third auxiliary (contemplation) for one who has that (knowledge), as in the case of knowledge and the rest.

verses.sanskrit: पाठभेद श्रुतेश्च added to 3.4.46 ॐ कृत्स्नभावात्तु गृहिणोपसंहारः ॐ
verses.transliteration: pAThabheda shruteshcha ## added to 3.4.46## OM kR^itsnabhAvAttu gR^ihiNopasaMhAraH OM
verses.translation: Because of its completeness, (the Chandogya text) concludes with the householder.
Silence (is enjoined) for others also, because of the teaching.
(He should live) without showing himself, because of the sequence (in the text).
In this life (the fruit comes), if there is no obstruction; so it is seen.
So there is no rule as to the fruit of liberation; the state (of liberation) is determined (as the same); the state is determined.

verses.sanskrit: अथ चतुर्थोऽध्यायः॥ ॐ आवृत्तिः असकृदुपदेशात् ॐ
verses.transliteration: atha chaturtho.adhyAyaH|| OM AvR^ittiH asakR^idupadeshAt OM
verses.translation: Repetition (of the meditation is required), because of the repeated teaching.
And because of the indication.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ आत्मेति तूपगच्छन्ति ग्राहयन्ति च ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM Atmeti tUpagachChanti grAhayanti cha OM
verses.translation: But (the texts) accept it as the Self, and teach (others) to grasp it so.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ न प्रतीके न हि सः ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM na pratIke na hi saH OM
verses.translation: Not in a symbol (should one see the Self), for (the meditator) is not that.
(In symbols) one should see Brahman, because of the elevation (of the symbol).
And the ideas of the sun and the like are to be superimposed on the (ritual) member, because that is reasonable.
One should meditate seated, because that is possible.
And because meditation (requires it).
And with reference to the immobility (of the meditator).
And the Smriti says so.
(Meditation may be practised) wherever concentration is attained, because there is no distinction.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ आ प्रायणात्तत्रापि हि दृष्टम् ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM A prAyaNAttatrApi hi dR^iShTam OM
verses.translation: Until death (meditation is to be continued); for it is seen (in scripture) even then.
On the attainment of that (Brahman), there follows the non-clinging of later sins and the destruction of former ones, because of the declaration.
The same holds for the other (good works): non-clinging; but at death (the body falls).

verses.sanskrit: ॐ अनारब्धकार्ये एव तु पूर्वे तदवधेः ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM anArabdhakArye eva tu pUrve tadavadheH OM
verses.translation: But only the former works, whose effect has not yet begun, (are destroyed), because of the limit (until death).

verses.sanskrit: ॐ अग्निहोत्रादि तु तत्कार्यायैव तद्दर्शनात् ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM agnihotrAdi tu tatkAryAyaiva taddarshanAt OM
verses.translation: But the Agnihotra and the like (continue) only for the sake of that (knowledge), as scripture shows.
Others hold that works other than these also (assist), of both kinds.
Because (the text says) "whatever is done with knowledge."

verses.sanskrit: ॐ भागेन त्वितरे क्षपयित्वा सम्पत्स्यते ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM bhAgena tvitare kShapayitvA sampatsyate OM
verses.translation: But having exhausted the other two (kinds of works) by experiencing them, he attains (Brahman).

verses.sanskrit: इति श्रीमत्कृष्णद्वैपायनकृतब्रह्मसूत्रेषु चतुर्थाध्यायस्य प्रथमः पादः समाप्तः ॐ वाङ्ग्मनसि दर्शनाच्छब्दाच्च ॐ
verses.transliteration: iti shrImatkR^iShNadvaipAyanakR^itabrahmasUtreShu chaturthAdhyAyasya prathamaH pAdaH samAptaH OM vA~Ngmanasi darshanAchChabdAchcha OM
verses.translation: Speech merges in the mind, because of what is seen and because of the text.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ अत एव च सर्वाण्यनु ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM ata eva cha sarvANyanu OM
verses.translation: For that very reason all (the organs) follow (into the mind).
That mind (merges) in prana, because of the later text.
That (prana merges) in the soul, the ruler, because of (the soul's) approach and other texts.
(The soul with prana merges) in the elements, according to scripture.
Not in one (element) only, for (the texts) show this.
The going is the same (for both) up to the beginning of the path; and immortality (is attained) without burning the subtle body.
(The subtle body lasts) until the merging in (Brahman), because worldly existence is stated.
The subtle (body) is minute in measure and nature, because it is so perceived.
Hence it is not destroyed by the burning (of the gross body).
And the warmth (of a living body) belongs to this (subtle body) alone, because that is reasonable.
If it be said that (the soul does not depart) because of the denial — no, (the denial concerns) the embodied soul (of the knower).
For it is clear (in the texts) of some (recensions).
And it is stated in the Smriti.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ तानि परे तथा ह्याह ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM tAni pare tathA hyAha OM
verses.translation: Those (elements and organs merge) in the Supreme; for so scripture says.
(They become) undivided (in Brahman), because of the statement.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ तदोकोऽग्रज्वलनं तत्प्रकाशितद्वारो विद्यासामर्थ्यात्तच्छेषगत्यनुस्मृतियोगाच्च हार्दानुगृहीताः शताधिकया ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM tadoko.agrajvalanaM tatprakAshitadvAro vidyAsAmarthyAttachCheShagatyanusmR^itiyogAchcha hArdAnugR^ihItAH shatAdhikayA OM
verses.translation: The front of his abode lights up; by that the door is illumined; through the power of knowledge and the recollection of the way (a part of the knowledge), and by the grace of the one within the heart, (he departs) by the channel exceeding a hundred.
(He goes) following the rays (of the sun).

verses.sanskrit: ॐ निशि नेति चेन्न संभन्धात् ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM nishi neti chenna saMbhandhAt OM
verses.translation: If it be said that (he does not go) at night — no, because of the connection (with the rays).

verses.sanskrit: पाठभेद 4.2.19 and 20 combined ॐ यावद्देहभावित्वाद्दर्शयति च ॐ
verses.transliteration: pAThabheda ## 4.2.19 and 20 combined ## OM yAvaddehabhAvitvAddarshayati cha OM
verses.translation: Because that connection lasts as long as the body does; and scripture shows it.
And for this reason (he attains) even when the sun is in the southern course.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ योगिनः प्रति स्मर्यते स्मार्ते चैते ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM yoginaH prati smaryate smArte chaite OM
verses.translation: (These times) are mentioned in the Smriti for yogis, and those rules belong to Smriti (not to the knower).

verses.sanskrit: इति श्रीमत्कृष्णद्वैपायनकृतब्रह्मसूत्रेषु चतुर्थाध्यायस्य द्वितीयः पादः समाप्तः ॐ अर्चिरादिना तत्प्रथितेः ॐ
verses.transliteration: iti shrImatkR^iShNadvaipAyanakR^itabrahmasUtreShu chaturthAdhyAyasya dvitIyaH pAdaH samAptaH OM archirAdinA tatprathiteH OM
verses.translation: (The knowers go) by the path of light and the rest, because that is well known.
(Vayu, the wind, is placed between the year and the sun,) because of the word "wind," from the general and specific statements.
Varuna (comes) after lightning, because of the connection.
(These are) conducting deities, because of the indication.
(They are conducting deities) because of the bewilderment of both (the soul and the organs on departure), which establishes that.
From there (the soul is led) by the being of lightning alone, because scripture says so.
Badari holds that (the soul is led to) the effect (Hiranyagarbha), because going is appropriate only to that.
And because of the specific qualification.
But it is called (Brahman) because of nearness.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ कार्यात्यये तदध्यक्षेण सहातः परमभिधानात् ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM kAryAtyaye tadadhyakSheNa sahAtaH paramabhidhAnAt OM
verses.translation: At the dissolution of the effect-world, (the soul goes) together with its ruler to the Supreme beyond, because of the statement.
And because of the Smriti.
Jaimini holds that (the soul goes to) the Supreme, since that is the primary (sense of Brahman).
And because scripture shows this.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ न च कार्ये प्रतिपत्त्यभिसन्धिः ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM na cha kArye pratipattyabhisandhiH OM
verses.translation: And there is no intention of attaining the effect (the Brahma-world) in the texts.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ अप्रतीकालम्बनान्नयतीति बादरायणरुभयथा च दोषात् तत्क्रतुश्च ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM apratIkAlambanAnnayatIti bAdarAyaNarubhayathA cha doShAt tatkratushcha OM
verses.translation: Badarayana holds that he leads those who do not rely on symbols, because of the faults in both (other views), and because of (the rule) that one becomes what one meditates on.
And scripture shows the difference.

verses.sanskrit: इति श्रीमत्कृष्णद्वैपायनकृतब्रह्मसूत्रेषु चतुर्थाध्यायस्य तृतीयः पादः समाप्तः ॐ सम्पद्याविहाय स्वेनशब्दात् ॐ
verses.transliteration: iti shrImatkR^iShNadvaipAyanakR^itabrahmasUtreShu chaturthAdhyAyasya tR^itIyaH pAdaH samAptaH OM sampadyAvihAya svenashabdAt OM
verses.translation: (The soul,) having attained (the highest light), manifests (its own nature), because of the word "own."
(It is) the liberated one, because of the declaration.
(The manifested nature is) the Self, because of the context.
(It is) undivided (from Brahman), because that is seen.
Jaimini holds that (it manifests) with the qualities of Brahman, because of the mention of such qualities and so on.
Audulomi holds that (it manifests) as mere consciousness, since that is its nature.
Badarayana holds that there is no contradiction even so, because of the mention (of both) and because of the earlier state (behind the two views).
And (the desired objects come) by will alone, because scripture says so.
For this very reason the liberated one has no other lord.
Badari says that he has no body (or organs); for scripture says so.
Jaimini holds that he has (a body), because of the alternative statements.
Badarayana holds that it is of both kinds, like the Dvadasaha rite.
In the absence of a body (he has enjoyments) as in dream, which is reasonable.
When there is a body, (they are) as in the waking state.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ प्रदीपवदावेशः तथा हि दर्शयति ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM pradIpavadAveshaH tathA hi darshayati OM
verses.translation: (He can enter several bodies) like a lamp (whose flame divides); for so scripture shows.
(The texts on "oneness") refer to either deep sleep or the attainment (of Brahman); for it is made manifest.
(The liberated have all powers) except the activity of creating the world.

verses.sanskrit: पाठभेद 4.4.17 and 18 combined ॐ प्रकरणादसन्निहितत्वाच्च ॐ
verses.transliteration: pAThabheda ## 4.4.17 and 18 combined ## OM prakaraNAdasannihitatvAchcha OM
verses.translation: Because of the context (which concerns the Lord alone), and because (the liberated) are not present (in the creation texts).
If it be said (that the liberated too may have lordship) because of the direct teaching — no, because it is said of those stationed in the spheres of office.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ विकारावर्ति च तथा हि दर्शयति ॐ
verses.transliteration: OM vikArAvarti cha tathA hi darshayati OM
verses.translation: And (the Lord) is also not subject to modification; for so scripture shows.
(Scripture) speaks of his abiding (in the Lord's nature); and thus Sruti and Smriti show.
And because of the indication of equality (with the Lord) in enjoyment alone.
There is no return — so declare the scriptures; no return — so declare the scriptures.
verses.hindi: पुनर्जन्म नहीं — शास्त्र ऐसा कहते हैं; पुनर्जन्म नहीं — शास्त्र ऐसा कहते हैं।
verses.wordMeaning: The final sutra of the Brahma Sutra repeats itself for emphasis: the liberated soul does not return. This is the ultimate fruit of brahma-jijnasa — the cycle of birth and death is ended for the one who has realised the Self. The repetition signals the conclusion of the entire treatise: from "athato brahmajijnasa" (now let us inquire) to "anavrittih shabdat" (there is no return) is the complete arc of the spiritual journey.
